clue.text: Common talent, in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: Common talent, in a manner of speaking

parts.words: Common talent, in a manner of speaking
parts.note: a widespread knack that is literally a way of talking: fluency and persuasiveness in speech

explanation.surface: Someone muses that an ordinary ability is, so to say, a talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' reads as a throwaway hedge, but it describes the talent itself: a gift for speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a natural fluency with words, a talent shown in one's manner of speaking.

clue.text: Showing enterprise he' takes a driver out

indicators.note: the driver word stands outside, enclosing the other two pieces

parts.note: a goad is a pointed stick for driving cattle

explanation.surface: An enterprising man takes a golfer's club out onto the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a golf club or motorist, but it is the cattle prod; 'out' means outside, so it surrounds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead person or firm is enterprising and keen to make progress.

clue.text: Overtime payment they understand

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service
read as 'over time': T, the abbreviation for time, comes below the payment in this down answer

explanation.surface: Workers grasp how overtime pay works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overtime' splits into 'over' plus 'time', putting FEE above T. 'They understand' is a joke definition: these are what we stand on, so they under-stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet are literally what stand underneath a person, so they 'under-stand' in a punning sense.

clue.text: Notably eccentric style

parts.note: 'Notably' hints at musical notes: a rhythm stressing the weak beats, and also unconventional

explanation.surface: Someone's dress sense is remarkably odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notably' looks like 'remarkably' but points to music: a style off the beat, which also means eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional things are called this, and in music it is a rhythm with stress on the normally weak beats.

clue.text: Yet a rat may be such a carrier

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder could be, after rearrangement, the carrier described

explanation.surface: A rodent might, oddly, turn out to be a carrier of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' tells you to rearrange YET A RAT; the rat and its plague-carrying reputation are pure misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat board with raised edges carries cups and pots for afternoon refreshment.

clue.text: She takes port during seasickness

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'She takes port during seasickness', gives no parse for ELSE: no word set gives E-L-S-E around L for port; likely OCR garble or misplaced clue.

clue.text: Crawler found inland around the Orient

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: E is east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A creeping creature is discovered inland, near the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange INLAND with E (the Orient, east); 'found' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthworms and leeches are segmented worms of this phylum, creatures that crawl.

clue.text: Curse these hot places!

parts.note: an oath like 'damn' followed by a word for very hot enclosures: the two run together name industrial smelting plants

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a sweltering spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an exclamation, it is 'Blast!' said of furnaces: the oath and the hot places together name the iron-smelting works.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is smelted in tall furnaces driven by a forced draught of hot air, the 'blast'.

clue.text: Where to find a rehash of Reade's stories

indicators.note: a rehash reworks old material, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the possessive S is kept here as a letter: READES

explanation.surface: Somewhere you would come across reworked tales by the novelist Charles Reade.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of READE'S STORIES, keeping the S. 'Where to find' is the definition: a place you go.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal holiday town is a place to go, somewhere to find holidaymakers.

clue.text: Granted it's time to be off

definitions.text: Granted it's time to be off

parts.words: Granted it's time to be off
parts.note: permission given for a period away from work or duty

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that it is time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Granted' looks like 'admittedly', but it means formally allowed: time off that has been granted.
explanation.definitionFit: This is authorised time away from one's post, permission granted for an absence.

clue.text: See 9
Staunch supporter

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to staunch is to stop a flow, as of blood
the stalk that holds up a leaf or flower

explanation.surface: A loyal backer stands firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' reads as the adjective 'loyal' but is the verb meaning to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop a flow is to check it, and a plant stalk holds up the bloom.

clue.text: He's got a bird on the line

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece placed on another comes first

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A man has a bird on a fishing line or on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: a man's name. RY is a common abbreviation for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a man's given name, so a male, 'he'.

clue.text: Records a leading range

indicators.note: the A goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records

explanation.surface: Someone documents a top selection of products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' looks like a verb; it is LPS, long-playing records.
explanation.definitionFit: The great European mountain range spans Switzerland, Austria and neighbours.

clue.text: I'll get by without a boiler in the outback

indicators.note: here means outside: the two letters of by surround the other word

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, giving three letters

explanation.surface: Someone says they'll manage without a heating boiler in the Australian bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, as in old usage. The Australian outback is the remote interior; there a billycan is the tin for boiling water over a campfire.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a billycan is a metal can used for boiling water or making tea over a fire.

clue.text: Striking Roman goddess

definitions.meaning: a type of short match that is struck to light
the Roman goddess of the hearth

explanation.surface: A Roman goddess is remarkably beautiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like 'impressive' but refers to a match, which you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax match was named after the hearth deity, so both senses share the name.

clue.text: Whimsical character with sum in hand

indicators.note: the sum word goes inside the hand word

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
to add is to sum

explanation.surface: An eccentric person stands holding a calculation in their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link word; 'sum' is a verb here, not a total.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows passing crazes or whims is a follower of fads.

clue.text: Gave up, gave in, gave way

definitions.meaning: let others go first, as at a junction

explanation.surface: Someone describes capitulating three ways over.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions of the same word in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Each phrase is a sense of the verb: surrendered, submitted and allowed traffic priority.

clue.text: Determination soldiers love to display

parts.note: REs, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: the word love is shown in a rearranged form

explanation.surface: Troops like showing their grit.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) plural gives RES; 'to display' rearranges LOVE into OLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is firmness of purpose, a synonym of determination.

clue.text: Point tone intent, say, to run

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
a camper is someone who sleeps in a tent

explanation.surface: A cue for someone sleeping under canvas to dash off.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'tone intent' is a scan misreading of 'one in tent'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly with small steps, like a child or small animal.

clue.text: Name he spelt wrongly

indicators.note: the letters are set out wrongly, in another order

explanation.surface: A man has misspelt someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange HE SPELT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Scottish form of Elizabeth, a woman's given name.

clue.text: But the pop singer could take heart from him

parts.note: taken as written
Cher is a famous American pop singer

explanation.surface: A fan might draw courage from a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take heart' means gain courage, but here it is literal: buying a heart, as offal, from a meat trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat seller sells organs such as heart, so customers take heart from him.

clue.text: Spirits raised by Ursa major and minor?

definitions.text: Spirits raised by Ursa major and minor?

parts.words: Spirits raised by Ursa major and minor?
parts.note: the Great and Little Bear constellations sit high in the sky, so the bears are up, and the idiom means keeps spirits up

explanation.surface: A question about whether star constellations cheer people up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ursa Major and Ursa Minor are the Great and Little Bear constellations, overhead in the sky; the phrase also means stays cheerful under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who copes cheerfully under hardship keeps their spirits raised.

clue.text: Repairs house in distasteful style

indicators.note: repairing a thing puts its parts back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fixing up a home in an unpleasant fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repairs' looks like a noun; it rearranges HOUSE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked or odious acts are deeply distasteful and shocking.

clue.text: Minder with a defiant expression

parts.note: yah is a derisive exclamation of defiance

explanation.surface: A carer speaks with a rebellious tone.
explanation.walkthrough: YAH is a jeering cry; 'with' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: In India an ayah is a nursemaid or children's nanny, someone who minds them.

clue.text: Indian state with a reciprocal service

indicators.note: going back the other way, so the service word is turned round

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: An Indian region offers mutual help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reciprocal service' looks like mutual aid; it is MASS, the church service, turned backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-eastern territory of India is famous for its tea.

clue.text: Register disapproval as he makes his point

parts.note: S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A man boos to make his position plain.
explanation.walkthrough: HIS then a compass point S; 'as he makes' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences make a sibilant sound to show they dislike a performance.

clue.text: Laurels for horses

definitions.meaning: bay trees, whose leaves made victory wreaths

explanation.surface: Victory wreaths for racehorses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' just joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree is a laurel, and reddish-brown horses with black manes are so called.

clue.text: Came out at the highest point

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Something emerged at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CAME.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or zenith of achievement is its summit.

clue.text: Atone for a tip out in a West-country river

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the river name

parts.note: the Exe flows through Devon in south-west England

indicators.note: the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Making amends for a gratuity lost in a river in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A TIP into PIAT. The West Country is south-west England, where the river flows through Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a sin is to make amends for it.

clue.text: Help in a sweet-sounding way

indicators.note: the word is said, giving the sound of another spelling

parts.note: a sucker is a lollipop, a sweet

explanation.surface: Offering help in a melodious manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet-sounding' looks like melodious but means a word for a sweet, said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is assistance given in time of need.

clue.text: Non-playing members of the cricket family

definitions.text: Non-playing members of the cricket family

parts.words: Non-playing members of the cricket family
parts.note: cricket the insect, not the sport: its relatives do not play the game

explanation.surface: Relatives of cricketers who don't play.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a bat-and-ball sport in Britain, but here it is the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: These jumping insects are close relatives of crickets, not players of the game.
